node.title: Unreduced DLI coset endpoint counterexample and primitive-scope repair
node.statement: At the admissible rate-half row n=2^41, t=2^33 and the printed Proth-certified prime q<2^256 with n dividing q-1, more than 2^127 central t-null subsets are unions of the 128 quotient fibers. Their unreduced normalized mass is greater than 2^126, so the unreduced endpoint X<=2^121 is false. Every witness is quotient-periodic and nonprimitive; therefore the DLI consumer and C2'' premise must use X_prim=q^{-t+H}W_cen^prim=E_U[product rho_j]_reduced after first-owner removal of the structured quotient column.
node.attack_surface: Check the Proth certificate, geometric-sum vanishing, central count, normalization inequality, and primitive ownership independently.
node.falsifier: A failed Proth congruence, a power-sum r<=t not annihilated by a quotient fiber, an incorrect half-band count, failure of the exact Bernoulli margin, or a witness that is primitive.
node.notes: The prior pilot used a BPSW probable-prime exhibit and counted the full quotient atom. This node replaces both gaps with a Proth certificate and the exact central half-band count. It refutes only the unreduced interface, not the primitive DLI residue.
